content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working on a project with three [product_name] modules over an Ethernet network, using [product_name] V[version_no]. My question is fairly basic—I'm not very experienced with [product_name] software. Given the two modes (diagram mode and network project mode), I want to write my program only in ladder logic. In diagram mode, I can select the ladder language, but in network mode, that option doesn't appear when I'm writing code. I realize this might be straightforward, but even after searching extensively, I haven't solved it. Maybe it's just not possible to use network input and output in diagram mode with ladder logic. Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you and regards,
As far as I know, only function block diagrams (FBD) can be used in network projects, not ladder logic.

Thank you for the quick response, [user_name]. I’ll keep trying. What options do I have for ladder logic? For simple programs, FBD is fine, but with more complex logic, I struggle with FBD. Is it possible to write the program in diagram mode using ladder logic, convert it to FBD, and copy it over to a network project? Will that preserve the intended logic? Regards,

You can convert a ladder diagram to an FBD diagram, but it doesn't always work perfectly. If you try to import a [product_name] in a network project, you'll notice that only FBD is available as an option, not ladder logic. Since I personally prefer FBD due to its functionality and reliability, I can't help with LAD. My recommendation: Learn to program using FBD.

Thank you for your reply, [user_name]. Learning FBD would be beneficial, but I’m not sure I’ll pursue it immediately. So, just to confirm: diagram mode allows ladder logic for programming a single [product_name], correct? Thanks and best regards,
With ladder logic, you can crosslink two [product_name] devices. You need to manually set the connections: configure one device as a client and the other as a server.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users find that using ladder logic in network project mode in [product_name] V[version_no] is not supported; only function block diagram (FBD) is allowed. This limitation frustrates those who prefer or are more comfortable with LAD. Attempts to convert ladder diagrams to FBD for use in network projects are unreliable and may introduce logic errors, raising usability concerns regarding language flexibility and compatibility between diagram types.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to program with ladder logic within network projects in the software, and to be able to transfer ladder logic-based programs into a network project easily and reliably.
pain_keywords: LAD not available in network projects
